note: Curated by hand. Every URL, package and flag was checked against the vendor's repo or docs on the verifiedAt date. Effort, time-saved and frequency values are editorial estimates, not measurements.

entries.name: GitHub MCP Server
entries.description: GitHub's official MCP server: issues, pull requests, code search, Actions runs and security alerts.
entries.problem: Reading a PR, its review comments, linked issues and failing checks means jumping between the browser, git and the terminal.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to open PR #123, read the diff and review threads, check why the Actions run failed and draft fixes in the same session.
benefits: Read issues, PRs, reviews and Actions logs from the agent
Search code across the org
Fewer context switches during review

access.summary: Whatever the token allows: repos, issues, PRs, Actions, alerts. stackhint configures the read-only mode by default.

auth.detail: Personal access token in GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN. Use a fine-grained token limited to the repos you need.

entries.network: Remote server at api.githubcopilot.com operated by GitHub.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_PAT"

codex.officialCommand: codex mcp add github --url https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ --bearer-token-env-var GITHUB_PAT_TOKEN

notes: Toolsets can be narrowed with the X-MCP-Toolsets header (default: context, repos, issues, pull_requests, users).

limitations: Lockdown mode is a best-effort filter, not a security boundary (GitHub's docs).
securityNotes: Issue and PR text is untrusted input to the agent; keep tool approvals on for write tools.

entries.name: GitHub CLI (gh)
entries.description: GitHub's command-line tool. Agents can call it from the shell for PRs, issues, checks and the REST/GraphQL API.
entries.problem: Without gh the agent cannot read PRs, checks or issues from the terminal.
entries.workflow: The agent runs `gh pr view 123 --comments`, `gh pr checks` and `gh run view --log-failed` instead of you copying output from the browser.
benefits: No MCP server and no extra context in every session
Uses your existing gh login
Works in both Claude Code and Codex through the shell

access.summary: Acts as your gh login; the agent's shell commands still need your approval.

guide: Install from https://cli.github.com (winget install GitHub.cli, brew install gh, or your distro package).

entries.name: GitLab MCP server
entries.description: MCP server built into GitLab (GA since 19.5, Free tier since 19.2): merge requests, work items, pipelines, repository.
entries.problem: Merge request review and pipeline debugging mean switching to the GitLab UI.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to read MR !42 with its discussions, look at the failed pipeline job and propose a fix.
benefits: Merge requests, work items and pipelines from the agent
OAuth, no long-lived token needed

access.summary: Acts as the signed-in user within project permissions. GitLab has no read-only mode for it.

auth.detail: OAuth with the 'mcp' scope, or a fine-grained PAT. Legacy PATs are rejected.

prerequisites: MCP access allowed for your top-level group or instance

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add -s user --transport http GitLab https://<gitlab.example.com>/api/v4/mcp

codex.officialCommand: codex mcp add GitLab --url "https://<gitlab.example.com>/api/v4/mcp" && codex mcp login GitLab
codex.notes: After adding, run `codex mcp login gitlab`.

limitations: gitlab.com rate limits: 60 requests/min on Free, 600 on Premium/Ultimate, shared across your clients.

entries.name: GitLab CLI (glab)
entries.description: GitLab's official command-line tool for merge requests, issues and pipelines.
entries.problem: Without glab the agent cannot read merge requests or pipelines from the shell.
entries.workflow: The agent runs `glab mr view 42 --comments` and `glab ci view` while it works.
benefits: No MCP server needed
Uses your existing glab login

access.summary: Acts as your glab login.

guide: Install glab from https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli#installation and run `glab auth login`.

entries.name: Atlassian Rovo MCP Server
entries.description: Atlassian's hosted MCP server for Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket Cloud.
entries.problem: Ticket details, acceptance criteria and linked Confluence pages live outside the repo, so you paste them into the chat by hand.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to read PROJ-123 with its comments and linked spec, implement it, then update the ticket.
benefits: Read and search Jira issues and Confluence pages
Link commits and branches to tickets without copy-paste

access.summary: Your Jira/Confluence permissions. There is no client-side read-only switch; admins control tool groups.

auth.detail: OAuth 2.1 in the browser; API tokens only if your org admin enables them.

entries.network: Remote server at mcp.atlassian.com. Atlassian Cloud only.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http atlassian https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp

codex.notes: After adding, run `codex mcp login atlassian` if the browser login does not start.

limitations: Cloud only: no Jira/Confluence Server or Data Center (use mcp-atlassian for those).
The old /v1/sse endpoint stopped working after 2026-06-30.
securityNotes: Ticket text is untrusted input to the agent.

entries.name: MCP Atlassian (community)
entries.description: Community MCP server for Jira and Confluence, including Server and Data Center, with a read-only mode.
entries.problem: Self-hosted Jira and Confluence are not covered by Atlassian's hosted MCP server.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to read an issue on your company's Jira Data Center and summarize the linked Confluence page.
benefits: Works with Jira/Confluence Server and Data Center
READ_ONLY_MODE blocks writes

access.summary: Whatever your API token allows; stackhint sets READ_ONLY_MODE=true by default.

auth.detail: JIRA_URL, JIRA_USERNAME and JIRA_API_TOKEN (Cloud) or JIRA_PERSONAL_TOKEN (Server/DC) in your environment.

entries.network: Runs locally and talks to your Jira/Confluence.

notes: Add CONFLUENCE_URL / CONFLUENCE_USERNAME / CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN to the server env if you also want Confluence.

limitations: Not an Atlassian product.
securityNotes: Prefer a token for a user with read access only, in addition to READ_ONLY_MODE.

entries.name: Linear MCP server
entries.description: Linear's hosted MCP server for issues, projects and comments.
entries.problem: Issue context sits in Linear while the code is in the editor.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to pick up ENG-412, read the issue and comments, and post a summary when the PR is ready.
benefits: Read and search Linear issues
Comment and update status (write mode)

access.summary: Your workspace data; stackhint uses the /mcp/readonly endpoint by default.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http linear-server https://mcp.linear.app/mcp

codex.officialCommand: codex mcp add linear --url https://mcp.linear.app/mcp && codex mcp login linear

limitations: The SSE endpoint is deprecated.

entries.name: Azure DevOps MCP Server
entries.description: Microsoft's MCP server for Azure DevOps: work items, repos and PRs, pipelines, wiki, test plans.
entries.statusNote: local package v2.10.0 (2026-09-09); remote server in preview
entries.problem: Work items, PR threads and pipeline logs are in Azure DevOps, away from the code.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to read work item 1234 and the failing pipeline run, then open a PR with the fix.
benefits: Work items, PRs, pipelines and wiki from the agent

access.summary: Your Azure DevOps permissions; the local server has no read-only mode.

auth.detail: Interactive Microsoft login on first use (default), or Azure CLI credentials.

entries.network: Runs locally (Node.js 20+) and talks to dev.azure.com.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport stdio azure-devops -- npx -y @azure-devops/mcp Contoso

codex.officialCommand: codex mcp add azure-devops -- npx -y @azure-devops/mcp Contoso
codex.notes: Codex cannot use the remote (Entra-only) server; the local one works.

limitations: The remote server needs an Entra-backed org and does not work with Codex.

entries.name: CircleCI MCP (hosted)
entries.description: CircleCI's hosted MCP server for pipelines, build logs and flaky tests.
entries.problem: Failed CircleCI builds mean opening the web UI and copying logs.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the last build on this branch failed; it reads the job log and test results and proposes a fix.
benefits: Build logs and test results in the agent
Flaky test detection

access.summary: Your CircleCI projects; rerun/cancel workflow tools change CI state.

auth.detail: OAuth2 in the browser (a token header works for headless use).

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http circleci-mcp-server https://mcp.circleci.com/v1/mcp

limitations: Preview or GA status is not stated in CircleCI's docs.

entries.name: Buildkite MCP Server
entries.description: Buildkite's MCP server for pipelines, builds, job logs and test suites.
entries.problem: Reading Buildkite job logs means leaving the editor.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to fetch the failing job log of the latest build and explain the failure.
benefits: Builds, jobs, logs and artifacts in the agent

access.summary: Builds can be created, retried or cancelled in write mode; stackhint uses the read-only endpoint by default.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http buildkite https://mcp.buildkite.com/mcp

entries.name: Jenkins MCP Server plugin
entries.description: Jenkins plugin that exposes jobs, builds and logs over MCP from your own controller.
entries.problem: Jenkins build logs are only in the Jenkins UI.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to read the last failed build log for this job and suggest a fix.
benefits: Builds and logs in the agent
Self-hosted: data stays on your controller

access.summary: Can trigger builds; limited by the Jenkins user's permissions. No read-only mode.

auth.detail: Jenkins user + API token as an HTTP Basic header, kept in JENKINS_MCP_AUTH (value: 'Basic <base64 user:token>').

prerequisites: The MCP Server plugin installed on Jenkins 2.541.3+ by an admin

limitations: Only useful if an admin installed the plugin on your controller.
securityNotes: Use a Jenkins account with limited permissions; there is no read-only mode.

entries.name: Context7
entries.description: Up-to-date, version-specific library documentation and code examples for the agent.
entries.problem: Models answer from training data and miss recent API changes in fast-moving libraries.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to use the current Next.js / Prisma / React Query API; it pulls the docs for the version you use before writing code.
benefits: Current docs for thousands of libraries
Fewer hallucinated or outdated APIs
No account needed

access.summary: Read-only documentation lookup. Your queries go to Context7's cloud.

auth.detail: None required; an optional API key raises rate limits.

entries.network: Remote server at mcp.context7.com. Library names and questions are sent there.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --scope user --transport http context7 https://mcp.context7.com/mcp

limitations: Context7 also offers a 'CLI + skills' mode (npx ctx7 setup) that uses fewer tokens than MCP.
securityNotes: Do not paste secrets into documentation questions.

entries.name: Microsoft Learn MCP Server
entries.description: Official Microsoft docs and code samples for .NET, Azure, Windows and more. Free, no login.
entries.problem: The agent guesses .NET and Azure APIs from memory, which goes stale every release.
entries.workflow: Ask how to configure rate limiting in ASP.NET Core 10; the agent searches Microsoft Learn, cites the page and uses the current API.
benefits: Searches and fetches official Microsoft docs
Code samples from Microsoft Learn
No account, read-only

access.summary: Read-only search of public Microsoft documentation.

entries.network: Remote server at learn.microsoft.com. Search queries are sent to Microsoft.
limitations: Public Microsoft documentation only.

entries.name: NuGet MCP Server
entries.description: Microsoft's NuGet server: package versions, vulnerable package fixes and package source mapping help.
entries.problem: Upgrading packages and fixing vulnerable dependencies means checking nuget.org and advisories by hand.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to update vulnerable packages in the solution; it checks nuget.org and edits the project files.
benefits: Current package versions from nuget.org
Fixes for vulnerable packages

access.summary: Reads your projects and can change package versions in project files.

entries.network: Runs locally via `dnx` and queries nuget.org.
limitations: Microsoft publishes no Claude Code or Codex instructions; the stdio command is the one from their docs.
Not version-pinned.

entries.name: DeepWiki MCP
entries.description: Questions and generated wiki pages about public GitHub repositories.
entries.problem: Understanding how an open-source dependency works internally means reading its source.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent how a library you depend on handles retries; it queries DeepWiki for that repo.
benefits: Explanations of public repos without cloning them
No account

access.summary: Read-only, public repositories only.

entries.network: Remote server at mcp.deepwiki.com; questions go to Cognition.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add -s user -t http deepwiki https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp

limitations: Public repositories only.

entries.name: Postgres MCP Pro
entries.description: PostgreSQL MCP server with a restricted (read-only) mode, EXPLAIN plans, index tuning and health checks.
entries.statusNote: Repo active (commits 2026-08), but the latest release is still v0.3.0 from 2025-05-16.
entries.problem: Debugging slow queries means copying schemas and EXPLAIN output between psql and the chat.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the orders query is slow; it reads the schema, runs EXPLAIN in a read-only transaction and suggests an index.
benefits: Schema inspection and EXPLAIN plans
Index and health recommendations
Restricted mode runs read-only transactions with time limits

access.summary: stackhint uses --access-mode=restricted (read-only transactions). Unrestricted mode can run any SQL including DDL.

auth.detail: Connection string in DATABASE_URI in your environment. Point it at a read-only database user.

entries.network: Runs locally and connects to your database.

prerequisites: A connection string, ideally for a read-only role

limitations: Release cadence is slow (last release May 2025).
securityNotes: Never point it at production with a privileged role; use a read-only role even in restricted mode.
Query results are sent to the model.

entries.name: DBHub
entries.description: Universal SQL MCP server by Bytebase: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle and SQLite.
entries.problem: Schema questions and query debugging need a live view of the database.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to find which tables reference customers and write the migration; it inspects the schema itself.
benefits: One server for most SQL databases
Schema exploration and SQL execution

access.summary: Runs arbitrary SQL. Read-only needs a dbhub.toml with readonly = true, which stackhint does not create; use a read-only database user.

auth.detail: Connection string in DSN in your environment (not on the command line).

entries.network: Runs locally and connects to your database.

prerequisites: A DSN for a read-only database user

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport stdio dbhub -- npx @bytebase/dbhub@latest --transport stdio --dsn "postgres://user:password@localhost:5432/dbname"

limitations: No read-only command-line flag.
securityNotes: The vendor examples put the password in --dsn on the command line; stackhint passes DSN through the environment instead.
Use a database user that can only SELECT.

entries.name: Supabase MCP Server
entries.description: Supabase's hosted MCP server: tables, SQL, logs, edge functions and project config.
entries.problem: Checking table data, RLS policies and logs means switching to the Supabase dashboard.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why a row-level security policy blocks a query; it reads the schema and policies in read-only mode.
benefits: Schema, data and logs from the agent
read_only=true runs queries as a read-only Postgres user

access.summary: stackhint adds read_only=true. Without it the agent can change your project.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --scope project --transport http supabase "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp"

notes: Add &project_ref=<id> to the URL to limit the server to one project.

limitations: Supabase says not to connect it to production data or expose it to end users.
securityNotes: Supabase warns about prompt injection through table data; keep tool approvals on.

entries.name: Neon MCP Server
entries.description: Neon's hosted MCP server: projects, branches, migrations and SQL on Neon Postgres.
entries.problem: Branching databases and testing migrations needs the Neon console.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to create a branch, apply the migration there and compare query plans.
benefits: Branches and migrations from the agent
readonly=true keeps SQL in read-only transactions

access.summary: stackhint adds readonly=true; without it the agent can manage projects and run any SQL.

auth.detail: OAuth in the browser, or a Neon API key header.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http neon https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp

limitations: Neon recommends it for development and testing, not production databases.
The /sse endpoint stopped working on 2026-10-01.

entries.name: ClickHouse MCP Server
entries.description: ClickHouse's MCP server for self-hosted ClickHouse. Read-only by default.
entries.problem: Analytical queries need schema knowledge the agent does not have.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to find why yesterday's events table has gaps; it lists tables and runs SELECTs.
benefits: List databases and tables, run SELECT queries
Writes stay disabled unless you enable them

access.summary: Read-only by default (CLICKHOUSE_ALLOW_WRITE_ACCESS=false).

auth.detail: CLICKHOUSE_HOST, CLICKHOUSE_USER and CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD in your environment.

entries.network: Runs locally and connects to your ClickHouse.
securityNotes: Use a ClickHouse user with readonly=1 as well.

entries.name: ClickHouse Cloud remote MCP server
entries.description: Hosted, always read-only MCP server for ClickHouse Cloud services.
entries.problem: Querying ClickHouse Cloud from the agent without managing credentials locally.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to compare this week's and last week's event counts; it runs SELECTs through the hosted server.
benefits: Always read-only
OAuth, no local credentials

access.summary: Always read-only (all tools are readOnlyHint).

auth.detail: OAuth in the browser; must be enabled per service in the Cloud console.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http clickhouse-cloud https://mcp.clickhouse.cloud/mcp

limitations: ClickHouse Cloud only.

entries.name: MongoDB MCP Server
entries.description: MongoDB's MCP server for databases and Atlas, with a read-only mode.
entries.problem: Inspecting collections and indexes means switching to Compass or mongosh.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to check which index the slow find() uses; it runs explain in read-only mode.
benefits: Collections, documents, indexes and explain plans
--readOnly registers only read tools

access.summary: stackhint uses --readOnly. Without it the agent can modify data and Atlas clusters.

auth.detail: Connection string in MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING in your environment.

entries.network: Runs locally and connects to your MongoDB.
securityNotes: MongoDB recommends secrets in environment variables, not command-line arguments.

entries.name: Redis MCP Server
entries.description: Redis's MCP server for keys, data structures, streams, JSON and vector search.
entries.problem: Debugging cache or queue contents means running redis-cli by hand.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent what is stored under the session:* keys and why they do not expire.
benefits: Inspect keys and data structures from the agent

access.summary: Full data access for the Redis user. No read-only flag; use an ACL user with +@read -@write.

auth.detail: REDIS_HOST, REDIS_PORT and optional REDIS_PWD in your environment.

entries.network: Runs locally and connects to your Redis.
limitations: stdio only.
securityNotes: Create an ACL user with read-only commands: ACL SETUSER readonlyuser on >password ~* +@read -@write.

entries.name: Kubernetes MCP Server
entries.description: MCP server for Kubernetes and OpenShift: resources, pod logs, events, optional Helm tools.
entries.problem: Debugging a deployment means running kubectl get/describe/logs and pasting output into the chat.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the api pod is crash-looping; it reads events, pod logs and the deployment spec.
benefits: Pods, logs, events and resources from the agent
Read-only mode for safe debugging

access.summary: stackhint passes --read-only (supported by the pinned v0.0.67). Without it the agent can delete resources and exec into pods.

auth.detail: Your kubeconfig (KUBECONFIG or ~/.kube/config). Prefer a context bound to a read-only ServiceAccount.

entries.network: Runs locally and talks to the clusters in your kubeconfig.

notes: The --read-only flag is removed on the project's main branch; the next release moves it to a TOML config (read_only = true). The version is pinned for that reason.

limitations: Not a Kubernetes/CNCF project.
Version 0.0.x.
securityNotes: Use a kubeconfig context with read-only RBAC; --read-only is defence in depth, not the boundary.

entries.name: Docker MCP Toolkit (MCP Gateway)
entries.description: Docker Desktop's catalog of containerized MCP servers behind one gateway, with its own client setup command.
entries.statusNote: MCP Toolkit is a Docker Desktop beta feature.
entries.problem: Running many MCP servers locally means managing many runtimes and secrets.
entries.workflow: Enable servers from Docker's catalog in Docker Desktop and connect Claude Code or Codex to the single gateway.
benefits: Each MCP server runs in its own container
One gateway entry instead of many

access.summary: Whatever the servers you enable in the profile can do.

auth.detail: Docker Desktop; secrets via `docker mcp secret`.

entries.network: Depends on the servers you enable.

prerequisites: Docker Desktop 4.62+ with the MCP Toolkit beta enabled

claude.officialCommand: docker mcp client connect claude-code

guide: Enable Settings > Beta features > Docker MCP Toolkit in Docker Desktop.
Run Docker's own command: `docker mcp client connect claude-code` or `docker mcp client connect codex`.
limitations: Beta.
Docker's command edits the client config itself; stackhint only shows it.

entries.name: Terraform MCP Server
entries.description: HashiCorp's MCP server for Terraform Registry docs (providers, modules, policies) and optionally HCP Terraform.
entries.problem: Provider resources and arguments change between versions; the agent writes HCL from memory.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to add an S3 bucket with versioning; it looks up the current aws provider docs before writing HCL.
benefits: Current provider and module docs
Registry lookups need no token

access.summary: Default config reads the public Terraform Registry only. With an HCP Terraform token it can manage workspaces.

auth.detail: None for public registry tools; TFE_TOKEN for HCP Terraform / Terraform Enterprise.

entries.network: Runs locally in Docker and queries registry.terraform.io.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add terraform -s user -t stdio -- docker run -i --rm hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server

codex.officialCommand: codex mcp add terraform -- docker run -i --rm hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server

entries.name: MCP for Argo CD
entries.description: Argo CD applications and resources over MCP, from the Argo Project Labs org.
entries.problem: Sync and health status of GitOps apps is only visible in the Argo CD UI.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the payments app is OutOfSync; it reads the app status and resource diffs.
benefits: Application status, resources and logs
MCP_READ_ONLY disables sync and delete

access.summary: stackhint sets MCP_READ_ONLY=true; otherwise it can sync, update and delete applications.

auth.detail: ARGOCD_BASE_URL and ARGOCD_API_TOKEN in your environment.

entries.network: Runs locally and talks to your Argo CD server.

entries.name: Flux MCP Server (flux-operator-mcp)
entries.description: MCP server for Flux GitOps resources from ControlPlane, with read-only mode and secret masking.
entries.problem: Flux reconciliation errors are scattered across Kustomizations, HelmReleases and sources.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the HelmRelease for ingress-nginx is not ready; it walks the Flux objects and events.
benefits: Flux and Kubernetes objects from the agent
Secrets masked by default

entries.network: Runs locally and talks to your clusters.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add flux-operator-mcp --env KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/config -- flux-operator-mcp serve

codex.officialCommand: codex mcp add flux-operator-mcp --env KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/config -- flux-operator-mcp serve

limitations: Not published by the CNCF Flux org.
AGPL-3.0 license.

entries.name: AWS MCP Server (managed)
entries.description: AWS's managed MCP server: AWS APIs under your IAM permissions plus AWS documentation search.
entries.problem: Checking deployed AWS resources and current AWS docs means switching to the console.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the Lambda times out; it reads the function config and CloudWatch logs and checks the docs.
benefits: AWS API calls and docs in one server
Calls are logged in CloudTrail

access.summary: Any AWS API your IAM principal allows. Restrict with IAM; the --read-only proxy flag needs the SigV4 setup.

entries.name: Azure MCP Server
entries.description: Microsoft's MCP server for Azure resources across many services, with a read-only mode.
entries.problem: Inspecting storage, Key Vault metadata or app config means the portal or long az commands.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent which app settings differ between staging and prod; it reads them with your az login in read-only mode.
benefits: Azure resources from the agent
--read-only blocks write operations

access.summary: stackhint passes --read-only; RBAC of your az login still applies.

auth.detail: Azure CLI login (az login) by default.

entries.network: Runs locally and calls Azure APIs.
limitations: First start downloads a large package.

entries.name: gcloud MCP server
entries.description: Google Cloud's MCP server that runs gcloud commands with your active credentials (preview).

entries.problem: Checking Cloud Run services, IAM or logs means the console or long gcloud commands.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to list Cloud Run revisions and find which one started failing.
benefits: gcloud from the agent with a built-in denylist

access.summary: Runs gcloud with your account's IAM rights (minus a denylist). No read-only flag.

auth.detail: Active gcloud credentials; Google recommends impersonating a limited service account.

entries.network: Runs locally and calls Google Cloud APIs.
limitations: Preview.
securityNotes: Use service-account impersonation with limited roles.

entries.name: Cloudflare API MCP Server
entries.description: Cloudflare's hosted MCP server for the whole Cloudflare API through two code-mode tools.
entries.problem: Workers, KV, D1 and DNS settings are in the Cloudflare dashboard.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to check the Worker's routes and recent errors before deploying.
benefits: The full Cloudflare API in about 1k tokens of tool definitions
Choose permissions at OAuth consent

entries.name: Vercel MCP
entries.description: Vercel's hosted MCP server: projects, deployments, logs and docs search.
entries.problem: Build and runtime logs of a failed deployment are in the Vercel dashboard.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the preview deployment failed; it reads the build logs and fixes the config.
benefits: Deployments and logs from the agent
Vercel docs search

access.summary: Same access as your Vercel user, including deploying. No read-only mode.

auth.detail: OAuth; only Vercel-reviewed clients (Claude Code and Codex CLI are on the list).

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http vercel https://mcp.vercel.com

entries.name: Firebase MCP server
entries.description: Firebase CLI's MCP server for Firestore, Auth, rules, hosting and more.
entries.problem: Firestore data and security rules are checked in the console.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to validate the Firestore rules against a sample document and fix the rule that blocks writes.
benefits: Firestore, Auth and rules tools from the agent

access.summary: Firebase project resources with your CLI login. No read-only mode; narrow with --only.

auth.detail: Firebase CLI login (firebase login) or Application Default Credentials.

entries.network: Runs locally and calls Firebase APIs.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add firebase npx -- -y firebase-tools@latest mcp

entries.name: Stripe MCP
entries.description: Stripe's hosted MCP server for the Stripe API and docs.
entries.problem: Checking customers, subscriptions and webhook events means the Stripe dashboard.
entries.workflow: In a sandbox, ask the agent why a webhook handler misses invoice.paid; it looks up recent events and the docs.
benefits: Stripe objects and docs search from the agent

access.summary: Most of the Stripe API, including refunds; Treasury tools can move money. Grant read-only permissions at OAuth consent.

auth.detail: OAuth per account or sandbox, or an Agent API key.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http stripe https://mcp.stripe.com/

limitations: From December 2026 Stripe stops accepting full-access secret keys and untagged restricted keys for MCP; migrate to OAuth or Agent API keys by 2026-11-30.
securityNotes: Use a sandbox account for agent work.
Refunds and outbound payments require human confirmation via URL.

entries.name: Sentry MCP
entries.description: Sentry's hosted MCP server: issues, events, traces and Seer analysis.
entries.problem: Stack traces and breadcrumbs for a production error are copied from Sentry by hand.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to fix the top unresolved issue; it pulls the stack trace and event context from Sentry first.
benefits: Issues, events and traces in the agent
OAuth, no token on disk

access.summary: Your Sentry org; some tools can update issues. No read-only switch.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/{organizationSlug}/{projectSlug}

limitations: Source-available license (FSL), not OSI open source.
securityNotes: Error payloads can contain user data; it goes to the model.

entries.name: Grafana MCP server
entries.description: Grafana's MCP server for dashboards, Prometheus/Loki queries, alerts and incidents.
entries.problem: Correlating a code change with metrics and logs means opening dashboards and writing PromQL by hand.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent whether latency went up after the last deploy; it queries Prometheus and Loki through Grafana.
benefits: Dashboards, datasource queries and alerts from the agent
--disable-write keeps it read-only

access.summary: stackhint passes --disable-write.

auth.detail: GRAFANA_URL and GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN in your environment.

entries.network: Runs locally and talks to your Grafana.

prerequisites: A Grafana service account token (Viewer role is enough for read-only)

limitations: For Grafana Cloud there is also a hosted server at mcp.grafana.com.

entries.name: Playwright MCP
entries.description: Microsoft's MCP server that drives a real browser through accessibility snapshots.
entries.problem: The agent cannot see what the UI actually renders, so frontend fixes are guesses.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to reproduce the checkout bug in a browser, read the page state and write a Playwright test for it.
benefits: The agent can click through your app
Turns a manual repro into a test

access.summary: Controls a browser that can open any site; file access limited to workspace roots by default.

entries.network: Runs locally; the browser goes wherever the agent navigates.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest

limitations: Playwright's README notes that coding agents may do better with the Playwright CLI plus skills, which uses fewer tokens.
securityNotes: Web pages are untrusted input; --allowed-origins is not a security boundary.

entries.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
entries.description: Google's MCP server for a live Chrome: console, network, performance traces, DOM.
entries.problem: Console errors, failing network calls and slow page loads are invisible to the agent.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the dashboard loads slowly; it records a performance trace and reads the network waterfall.
benefits: Console, network and performance data for the agent
Works with your running dev server

access.summary: Full control of a Chrome instance, including script execution.

entries.network: Runs locally. stackhint adds --no-usage-statistics because usage stats are sent to Google by default.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add chrome-devtools --scope user npx chrome-devtools-mcp@latest

codex.officialCommand: codex mcp add chrome-devtools -- npx chrome-devtools-mcp@latest

limitations: Chrome and Chrome for Testing only.
securityNotes: Performance tools may send trace URLs to Google's CrUX API unless --no-performance-crux is set.

entries.name: Postman MCP Server
entries.description: Postman's MCP server for workspaces, collections and environments.
entries.problem: API collections and environments live in Postman and drift from the code.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to update the Postman collection after changing an endpoint, or to generate a client from a collection.
benefits: Collections and environments from the agent

access.summary: Your Postman workspaces; no read-only mode.

auth.detail: OAuth (US region) or a Postman API key.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http postman https://mcp.postman.com/mcp

limitations: EU accounts must use mcp.eu.postman.com with an API key.

entries.name: SonarQube MCP Server
entries.description: SonarSource's MCP server for SonarQube Cloud/Server issues, quality gates and metrics.
entries.problem: Quality gate failures and Sonar issues have to be read in the Sonar UI.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to fix the issues blocking the quality gate on this branch.
benefits: Issues, hotspots and quality gate status in the agent
SONARQUBE_READ_ONLY=true

access.summary: stackhint sets SONARQUBE_READ_ONLY=true; without it the agent can change issue status.

auth.detail: SONARQUBE_TOKEN and SONARQUBE_ORG (Cloud) in your environment. SonarQube Server: set SONARQUBE_URL instead of SONARQUBE_ORG.

entries.network: Runs locally in Docker and talks to SonarQube Cloud or your server.
limitations: Source-available license (SSAL), not OSI open source.
Image tag not pinned (vendor uses --pull=always).

entries.name: Semgrep MCP (semgrep mcp)
entries.description: MCP server built into the Semgrep CLI for local security scans.
entries.problem: Security findings show up in CI after the code is written.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to scan the files it changed with Semgrep before committing and fix the findings.
benefits: Local SAST scans from the agent
No account needed for local rules

access.summary: Reads local code to scan it.

auth.detail: None for local scans; SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN for platform features.

entries.network: Runs locally; rule downloads come from semgrep.dev.
limitations: Minimum Semgrep version is not documented.

entries.name: Snyk MCP (snyk mcp)
entries.description: MCP server in the Snyk CLI for SCA, code, IaC and container scans.
entries.problem: Dependency and code vulnerabilities are reported after the fact.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to run a Snyk scan on the new dependency and pick a safe version.
benefits: Snyk scans from the agent

access.summary: Scans local folders and sends results to your Snyk account.

auth.detail: Browser login to Snyk; the folder must be trusted.

entries.network: Runs locally; scan data goes to Snyk.
limitations: Snyk's current setup path for Claude Code and Codex is their own installer script; this is the plain MCP route.

entries.name: Notion MCP (hosted)
entries.description: Notion's hosted MCP server for reading and editing workspace pages and databases.
entries.problem: Specs and runbooks live in Notion and get pasted into the chat.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to read the spec page linked in the README and implement the next section.
benefits: Search and read Notion pages from the agent

access.summary: Read, create and update content you can access. No read-only mode.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp

securityNotes: Page content is untrusted input to the agent.

entries.name: Figma MCP server
entries.description: Figma's hosted MCP server: design context, variables and components for implementing designs.
entries.problem: Implementing a design from screenshots loses spacing, tokens and component names.
entries.workflow: Paste a Figma frame link and ask the agent to build it with your components; it reads the real layout and variables.
benefits: Exact layout, variables and components from Figma

access.summary: Reads files you can access; write-to-canvas (beta) can modify designs.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http figma https://mcp.figma.com/mcp

limitations: Rate limits depend on your Figma plan and seat.

entries.name: C# language server plugin (csharp-lsp)
entries.description: Official Claude Code plugin that connects csharp-ls for go-to-definition, references and diagnostics.
entries.problem: Without a language server the agent finds symbols with grep and misses compiler errors until build.
entries.workflow: The agent jumps to definitions and sees diagnostics right after it edits a .cs file.
benefits: Go to definition and find references
Diagnostics after each edit

access.summary: Runs a local language server on your code.

guide: Install the language server: `dotnet tool install --global csharp-ls`.
In Claude Code: `/plugin install csharp-lsp@claude-plugins-official` (or `claude plugin install csharp-lsp@claude-plugins-official`).
limitations: Needs the csharp-ls executable on PATH.

entries.name: TypeScript language server plugin (typescript-lsp)
entries.description: Official Claude Code plugin that connects typescript-language-server.
entries.problem: Type errors show up only when the build runs.
entries.workflow: The agent sees type errors and references immediately after editing .ts/.tsx files.
benefits: Go to definition and find references
Type errors after each edit

access.summary: Runs a local language server on your code.

guide: Install the server: `npm install -g typescript-language-server typescript`.
limitations: Needs typescript-language-server on PATH.

entries.name: Python language server plugin (pyright-lsp)
entries.description: Official Claude Code plugin that connects Pyright for type checking and navigation.
entries.problem: Type errors in Python code surface only at runtime or in CI.
entries.workflow: The agent sees Pyright diagnostics right after editing .py files.
benefits: Go to definition and find references
Type diagnostics after each edit

access.summary: Runs a local language server on your code.

prerequisites: pyright (npm install -g pyright, pip install pyright or pipx install pyright)

guide: Install Pyright (`pipx install pyright` or `npm install -g pyright`).
limitations: Needs pyright-langserver on PATH.

entries.name: Go language server plugin (gopls-lsp)
entries.description: Official Claude Code plugin that connects gopls.
entries.problem: The agent navigates Go code by grep.
entries.workflow: The agent uses gopls for definitions, references and diagnostics after edits.
benefits: Navigation and diagnostics

access.summary: Runs a local language server on your code.

guide: Install gopls, then in Claude Code: `/plugin install gopls-lsp@claude-plugins-official`.

entries.name: Code Review plugin (code-review)
entries.description: Official Claude Code plugin: /code-review runs several review agents on a PR and posts only high-confidence issues.
entries.problem: Reviewing pull requests well takes time and is easy to rush.
entries.workflow: On a PR branch run /code-review; four agents check guidelines, bugs and history and post issues scored 80+.
benefits: Parallel review agents
Filters low-confidence noise

access.summary: Posts a review comment on the PR through your GitHub access.

guide: In Claude Code: `/plugin install code-review@claude-plugins-official`, then `/code-review` on a PR branch.
limitations: Posts a comment to the PR; run it only where that is welcome.

entries.name: A project skill for a repeated workflow
entries.description: Turn a workflow you repeat in this repo into a skill the agent loads on demand (SKILL.md), using the built-in skill creator.
entries.problem: The same multi-step change (a migration, a new endpoint, a release) is explained to the agent again every time.
entries.workflow: Write the steps, conventions and a template once in a skill; next time say 'add the Orders endpoint' and the agent follows it.
benefits: Consistent output for repeated tasks
Loaded only when needed, so no constant context cost
Lives in the repo and is shared with the team

access.summary: A Markdown file in your repo; it can include scripts you review.

codex.notes: Use the built-in $skill-creator; repo skills live in .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md.

guide: Claude Code: `/plugin install skill-creator@claude-plugins-official`, then ask: "use skill-creator to make a project skill for <the workflow>".
Codex: ask "$skill-creator make a repo skill for <the workflow>".
limitations: Worth it only for workflows you repeat at least a few times a month.
securityNotes: Review any scripts a skill runs before committing it.

entries.name: PostgreSQL reference server (@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres)
entries.description: The original reference Postgres server. Archived; its read-only guard can be bypassed.
entries.statusNote: Archived 2025-05-29. Datadog Security Labs showed a read-only bypass via multi-statement SQL (COMMIT; ...); v0.6.2 is unpatched.

access.summary: Intended read-only, but the guard is bypassable.

auth.detail: Connection URL as a command-line argument.

securityNotes: Read-only bypass via SQL injection (Datadog Security Labs, 2025-08-21).
